claim_en: THE FRAME: THESE ARE THE WORDS MOSES SPOKE TO ALL ISRAEL BEYOND THE JORDAN — IN THE WILDERNESS, IN THE ARABAH OPPOSITE SUPH, BETWEEN PARAN, TOPHEL, LABAN, HAZEROTH AND DI-ZAHAB — ELEVEN DAYS FROM HOREB TO KADESH-BARNEA; IN THE FORTIETH YEAR, THE ELEVENTH MONTH, THE FIRST OF THE MONTH, ACCORDING TO ALL THE LORD COMMANDED HIM, AFTER SMITING SIHON AND OG, MOSES UNDERTOOK TO EXPLAIN THIS TORAH. 'These are the words' five Bible seats; 'beyond the Jordan' eleven Torah seats, nine this book's; Suph a place (the Sea of Reeds two tokens at 1:40); Kadesh-barnea two tokens only here and 1:19; 'eleven days' one seat, the parser [11]; the date [40, 11, 1] by the number reader against Numbers 33:38's ordinal [40, 5] — one year, two forms, Aaron's death and this speech six months apart; 'ACCORDING TO ALL THAT THE LORD COMMANDED HIM' two seats with Exodus 40:16's tabernacle receipt — the Sifrei 2:8 reads it as the receipt of the hermeneutic rules themselves; 'explain' three seats (27:8, Habakkuk 2:2) by the consonants of 'well'. THE SIFREI 1 reads the six places as six sins (the ten trials, R. Judah; plain places named for events, R. Yose ben Dormaskit — the dispute held open at 1:18), and ONKELOS WRITES THAT READING INTO THE VERSE: 'he rebuked them for that they sinned in the wilderness, provoked opposite the Sea of Reeds, scorned the manna in Paran, provoked over the meat at Hazeroth, made the calf of gold' — thirty-three tokens for twenty-two, the book's one 'rebuked'. The Sifrei 2: eleven days become forty years, three days, one, none by merit; the year's twelve months from the date; the rebuke near death (Jacob, Joshua, Samuel, David). The Sifrei 3: after the victories lest they say he rebukes from weakness; king and province hard. The Sifrei 4: 'undertook' a beginning (R. Judah — Onkelos takes it) or an oath (the sages — 27:1 takes it); 'explain' — review before death.
middah: ink (the phrases', names' and forms' seats censused; the two date forms measured by the two readers; the translation's tokens counted against the verse's); the aggadic name-reading (Sifrei 1:9-17 — each place a charge) and I5 (1:1 — 'these words' against the whole Torah; 2:8 — 'all' the rules); I1 (3:3-4, king and province); E7 (4:1 — 'undertook' fixed from its other seats)

claim_en: HOREB: THE LORD OUR GOD SPOKE TO US AT HOREB — YOU HAVE DWELT LONG ENOUGH AT THIS MOUNTAIN; TURN AND JOURNEY TO THE HILL COUNTRY OF THE AMORITES AND ALL ITS NEIGHBORS, THE ARABAH, THE HILL, THE LOWLAND, THE NEGEB, THE COAST, THE LAND OF THE CANAANITE AND LEBANON, TO THE GREAT RIVER EUPHRATES; SEE, I HAVE SET THE LAND BEFORE YOU — GO IN AND POSSESS THE LAND SWORN TO ABRAHAM, ISAAC AND JACOB AND THEIR SEED. 'ENOUGH FOR YOU' eight Bible seats — Korah's twice (Numbers 16:3, 7), 1:6, 2:3, 3:19, Jeroboam's, Ezekiel's — and the singular once, 3:26 on Moses; Onkelos keeps the four; 'turn and journey' Numbers 14:25's words at their second seat; the five regions in one verse one seat; 'THE GREAT RIVER, THE RIVER EUPHRATES' Genesis 15:18's words at their second seat (Joshua 1:4 plene); 'see, I have set before you' one seat; the patriarchs' dative eleven Torah seats. The Sifrei 5: 'enough' as reward (the tabernacle, the Torah, the elders, the officers), benefit and harm — idleness; 6: the regions as Mishnah Sheviit 9:2's, Lebanon a king and the Temple (Onkelos writes the Temple at 3:25, keeps Lebanon here), the Euphrates' bulk toward the Land; 7: not by hearsay but what you see, no weapons but a surveyor; 8: each patriarch worthy alone, the Land given as-is and improved by each, the three datives three possessions (David and Jeroboam's; Rabbi: Babylon's returners and the Messiah's days).
middah: ink (the phrase's eight seats and the singular; the regions' and the river's seats; the dative triad's); the homonym read (Sifrei 5:2 — 'much' for 'enough'); E7 (6:2 — Lebanon fixed from Ezekiel and Jeremiah); I5 (8:1 — the triad resolved to three merits)

claim_en: I CANNOT BEAR YOU ALONE: THE LORD HAS MULTIPLIED YOU AS THE STARS OF HEAVEN — MAY HE ADD A THOUSAND TIMES AND BLESS YOU AS HE SPOKE; HOW CAN I BEAR ALONE YOUR TROUBLE, YOUR BURDEN AND YOUR STRIFE? GIVE YOURSELVES WISE AND UNDERSTANDING AND KNOWN MEN FOR YOUR TRIBES AND I WILL SET THEM AS YOUR HEADS. 'I cannot bear you alone' one seat — Numbers 11:14's cry and Jethro's 'you are not able alone' (Exodus 18:18) the kin; 'as the stars of heaven for multitude' three seats, all this book's; 'a thousand times' one seat, the parser [1000]; 'how' the Lamentations word, Genesis 3:9's 'where are you' by the consonants; 'your trouble' a hapax; 'give yourselves' four seats; the three qualities against Jethro's four (Exodus 18:21) and 1:15's two; 'and I will set them as your heads' one seat. Onkelos: 'bear' one root (1:9, 12, 31), 'your business and your judgments' for the burden and the strife. The Sifrei 9: not from myself; the judge liable in his person for a money error (Proverbs 22:23); 10: 'today' — you endure; the seven classes of the righteous; 11: 'a thousand times' Moses' bounded blessing, 'as he spoke' the LORD's unbounded (the guardian parable); 12: the troublesome litigant, the cynics who read Moses' every step, the disputatious; 13: 'give' is counsel, 'men' excludes women, wise against understanding (the two money-changers), 'known' to the tribes, the appointment Moses' alone — and READ NOT 'I will set them' BUT 'THEIR GUILT ON YOUR HEADS' (Ezekiel 33's watchman).
middah: ink (the clause's, the phrase's and the qualities' seats censused against Exodus 18); I2 (13:2 — 'men' excludes; 13:1 — 'give' fixed from 2 Samuel 16:20); the AL TIKREI (13:6 — the consonants revocalized: MOVE_CATALOG to check); the parable (11:1, 13:3)

claim_en: THE JUDGES CHARGED: HEAR BETWEEN YOUR BROTHERS AND JUDGE RIGHTEOUSLY BETWEEN A MAN AND HIS BROTHER AND HIS STRANGER; RECOGNIZE NO FACES IN JUDGMENT, HEAR SMALL AND GREAT ALIKE, FEAR NO MAN, FOR THE JUDGMENT IS GOD'S; THE HARD MATTER BRING TO ME — AND I CHARGED YOU ALL THE THINGS YOU SHOULD DO. 'His stranger' two Bible seats (Exodus 6:4 by the consonants); 'you shall not recognize faces' 1:17 and 16:19; 'small and great alike' the Torah's one seat; the fear-verb by its lemma (the store's sojourn-gloss corrected); 'for the judgment is God's' one seat; 'at that time' the refrain's ten. Onkelos: 'in truth' for 'righteously', 'the judgment is the LORD's'. The Sifrei 16: BE DELIBERATE IN JUDGMENT — Avot 1:1's saying seated here; the judges bound to the public (R. Yohanan ben Nuri and R. Elazar Hisma); R. Ishmael and the gentile litigant (Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel: by the law they chose); the righteous claimant brings proof against the holder; 'a man' excludes the minor — orphans are not judged; 'his brother' includes every pair; 'his stranger' the piler of claims, the neighbor, the groomsman, the lodger. 17: the prohibition on the APPOINTER of judges; the poor man's and the rich man's dignity refused; silence before hearing, none after; compromise a dispute (Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel for, the sages against — 'he who blesses a compromiser spurns the LORD'); fear of the litigant refused, 'the judgment is God's' (Jehoshaphat's charge); THE HARD MATTER — Zelophehad's daughters (Numbers 27, THE TENT's fourth sitting) and Samuel the seer. 18:1: the ten distinctions between money cases and capital cases (Sanhedrin 4:1).
